title: Firehall Breakfast Pizza
subtitle: Sheet-pan pizza loaded with scrambled eggs, sausage, and melty cheese.
description: Two large sheet-pan pizzas feed a full hall without a delivery driver. Pre-baked crusts get a layer of gravy-spiked white sauce, scrambled eggs, browned sausage, and cheddar—cut into squares for fast line service.

ingredients.name: shredded mozzarella
ingredients.notes: mixed into gravy for white sauce

ingredients.name: sliced green onions
ingredients.notes: and hot sauce at the line

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Firehall Breakfast Pizza in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Sausage. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Heat the ovens
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 425°F. Oil two half-sheet pans or large rimmed baking sheets. Stretch dough to fit each pan with a slight rim for toppings. Allow 10–15 minutes for mise en place before heat goes on. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Par-bake the crusts
steps.instruction: Dock dough with a fork, then par-bake 6–8 minutes until the surface sets but is not fully browned. This prevents a soggy middle once eggs and gravy go on. Bake until the center reaches a safe internal temp (165°F) and edges look set — use a thermometer at the thickest point. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Prep toppings
steps.instruction: Whisk gravy with mozzarella until smooth. Soft-scramble eggs over low heat—they should still look glossy. Brown sausage and drain on paper towels so the pizza doesn't weep grease. Plan about 12 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Build and bake
steps.instruction: Spread white gravy on par-baked crusts, dot with scrambled eggs and sausage, then blanket with cheddar. Bake until cheese bubbles and crust edges are deep golden. Bake until the center reaches a safe internal temp (165°F) and edges look set — use a thermometer at the thickest point. Plan about 14 minutes for this step at crew scale.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Rest and square-cut
steps.instruction: Rest pizzas 5 minutes on the pan so cheese sets. Cut into squares with a sharp pizza wheel or bench scraper. Hold warm at 200°F uncovered for crisp edges. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

stationWorkflow: One cook runs the oven rotation while another scrambles eggs and browns sausage in parallel.
Par-bake both crusts together, then build one pizza at a time so the second crust doesn't over-proof on the counter.
Cut on the sheet pan at the line and slide squares onto a warm hotel pan for self-serve portions.
cleanupNotes: Line sheet pans with parchment for easier release and faster scrub-down after cheese bakes on.
Soak pizza cutters and bench scrapers immediately—egg and cheese glue sets hard once cooled.
leftovers: Reheat squares on a sheet pan at 350°F for 8 minutes; avoid the microwave so crust stays crisp.
Dice cold squares into a breakfast strata base with extra eggs and milk for tomorrow's bake.
